title: Training vs. Validation Error -- Spotting the Overfitting Point
description: Slide through 50 training epochs and find the exact point where validation error turns upward.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Foundations
chapter_title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Foundations

educational.learningObjective: Given a live chart of training error and validation error over training time, the learner will identify the specific point where continued training begins to overfit the model, and explain why the two curves diverge after that point.
prerequisites: Knows that a model is trained on data
Can read a two-series line chart
learningOutcomes: Identify the overfitting point from two error curves
Explain why training error keeps falling after that point
Describe what early stopping does and why it works
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a pair of error curves and ask for the stopping epoch plus a one-sentence reason.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Slider playhead across two curves with a phase readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Confronting the intuition that more training is always better
pedagogical.feedbackType: Numeric values at the playhead plus a named phase and a computed marker
misconceptionsAddressed: That lower training error always means a better model
That overfitting shows up in the training error
discussionQuestions: Why does a model that fits the training data perfectly generalize badly?
What is the human equivalent of overfitting?
Why is holding out data an inconvenience worth paying for?
